lines.text: How does McDonald’s work?
Who runs it? Who decides? And who’s behind the counter?
Behind the brand you know, there’s a global organization.
At the top, a board of directors oversees governance.
The CEO and the executive team run the company day to day.
Around headquarters, major specialized functions: finance, marketing, operations,
human resources, technology, franchise development, legal.
Each has its own role, and they all coordinate their efforts.
Internationally, McDonald’s is organized through different structures:
operated markets, subsidiaries, licensed partners, affiliates.
Responsibilities vary by country.
In restaurants, the model relies on franchising.
The franchisee is an independent operator, bound by a contract and brand standards.
They run their own restaurant and their own teams.
Every restaurant starts with its operator.
The manager runs daily operations, supported by assistants,
shift managers, and versatile crew members.
The exact organization varies by country and restaurant.
Here’s the overall org chart.
At the top, governance and leadership; in the middle, functions and international.
On a separate branch, the franchisees; at the bottom, the teams.
McDonald’s: a global organization, thousands of entrepreneurs, local teams.
